key_insight: A scaffold-aware foundation model pretrained on small-molecule natural products uses masked objectives and contrastive learning to learn rich, transferable molecular representations. This improves taxonomy classification, genome mining linkage and virtual screening performance over baselines.
problem_solved: Existing molecular models are not optimized for the structural diversity and scaffold-centric biology of natural products, limiting accurate taxonomy assignment, linking molecules to biosynthetic genes/genomes, and reliable virtual screening for drug discovery.
method: Design a scaffold-aware encoder that explicitly models core scaffolds and substituents in molecule representations.
Pretrain with masked reconstruction objectives plus contrastive learning signals (molecule↔molecule and molecule↔taxonomy/genome) to align chemical and biological modalities.
Fine-tune the foundation model on downstream tasks: taxonomy classification, genome mining (biosynthetic gene cluster linking), and virtual screening.
impact: Provides an off-the-shelf, transferable pretrained model tailored to natural products, reducing labeled-data needs and boosting performance on key discovery tasks—accelerating AI-driven natural-product drug discovery workflows.

paper_title: Pretraining a foundation model for small-molecule natural products
paper_authors: Yuheng Ding, Bo Qiang, Shaoning Li, Yiran Zhou, Jie Yu
